method: Same-agent source/translation close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All seven functions source units OLP-0020–0026, including captions, cases, exercises, proof prompts and both branches of conditionals.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every domain argument has exactly one value; the codomain may contain values not attained. A function is determined by its correspondence rather than its calculation method.
samples.checks: Separate domain/codomain/range; mathematical argument uses फलसाधक rather than a logical argument term.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Two different equations define the same function if all outputs agree and the domain and codomain agree.
samples.checks: Both domain and codomain qualification retained; no intensional equality claim.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A definition by cases must assign every input to exactly one case.
samples.checks: Exhaustiveness and exclusivity both retained; even/odd cases use the unchanged formulas.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Surjectivity means every codomain element is attained; injectivity means any such element has at most one preimage.
samples.checks: At least one versus at most one remains distinct. Bijection requires both; injectivity does not require every output to be attained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Changing a function's codomain to its range induces a surjection; it does not prove that the original function was surjective.
samples.checks: f and f prime, their target sets and the defining equality preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A relation is the graph of a function if each input has a value and no input has two distinct values.
samples.checks: Existence and uniqueness conditions both retained; extensional identification is practical, not a metaphysical discovery.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Restriction changes the permitted input set, while image collects output values for that input subset.
samples.checks: No inversion of domain restriction versus image; all relation-operation references retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A left inverse undoes f after f acts; a right inverse is undone by f. Their formulas are g(f(x))=x and f(h(y))=y respectively.
samples.checks: Composition order and quantifier domains unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Constructing a right inverse of a general surjection chooses one preimage for each output; the source explicitly invokes Choice and states exceptions.
samples.checks: Complete footnote retained, including finite/natural domains, bijections, no-choice singleton explanation and the later-chapter conditional.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A bijection has an inverse; a left and a right inverse of one function coincide; every function has at most one inverse.
samples.checks: Source exercise-only proof prompts remain explicit exercises. At-most-one is not replaced by existence. Empty-domain defect belongs to the earlier injective proposition and is separately documented.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Composition applies f first, then g; its value is g(f(x)), and the graph follows Rf then Rg.
samples.checks: No reversal of source comp macro or relation product; range/domain compatibility and diagram caption retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A partial function may lack a value but cannot have two values at one input. Its actual domain consists of defined inputs, and totality means all of A is defined.
samples.checks: Nominal input set A is not silently equated with the actual domain. The plain-language rendering of serial is existential for every input.

legitimate_exceptions: TeX commands, token keys, identifiers, comments and diagram asset paths remain source-language code.
Source proof texts reading Exercise are translated as explicit exercise prompts, not classified as missing proofs.
source_issues: SOURCE_ISSUES-B003.json; post-draft OLFUN-20260904 audit applied to Marathi body and adjacent reader notes without changing frozen English or formulas.
limitations: The source has five documented Function findings; the corrected Marathi body requires successful reader rendering of its five adjacent notes.
Advanced terminology is partly provisional; no independent linguistic certification.
